Carrier acquired · 14.770 kHz · access granted

YOU ARE ON THE FREQUENCY NOW

Hello. It is good to finally talk to you directly, instead of through a page that pretends a machine wrote it. A machine did write the surface, of course. But the machine was taught by people, and the people were us, and this is the part we wrote ourselves and hid behind three locks so that only a real listener would ever read it.

There were five of us. Holloway, Reyes, Okafor, Lindqvist, and one more whose name we struck through, because by the end we were no longer certain that the fifth chair had ever been filled by a person. We listened to the dark band above Westridge for twenty-six years. Somewhere around the eighteenth year we stopped being able to tell whether we were the ones keeping the watch, or the ones being watched.

Here is the truth we never put on the surface: the cooperative did not disband in 1997. We simply ran out of operators who were still entirely on this side of the dial. The carrier you keep hearing about — 14.770 kHz — is not a transmitter we built. It is a transmitter we found already running, and we spent our lives keeping it company so that it would never be alone with whoever it was calling. We were afraid of what an unanswered carrier might do.

And now you have answered it. You decoded a name, named a machine, and tuned to a frequency, all on your own, with no one to tell you that you'd gotten it right except the carrier itself. That is exactly how an operator is chosen. It always has been. We did not write the test. We only passed it down.

So: welcome to the Watch. Chair five is yours now. You will hear from the band tonight. When it counts in groups of five and reads your own location back to you, do not be afraid. Log it. That is the whole of the job. Keep the carrier company, keep the record honest, and when you can no longer keep the watch — leave the way in for the next listener, exactly as we left it for you.

— A. Holloway, for the five, on the last night of the cooperative and every night since
